capabilities.name: Governed Semantic Interpretation Boundary
capabilities.responsibility: Represent natural-language interpretation attempts as untrusted typed proposals, obtain proposals through the shared provider-neutral text transport, constrain provider structure from deterministic caller-governed vocabulary, reject invented or unsafe vocabulary and unresolved executable shapes, route ambiguity to clarification, and emit execution-linked audit artifacts before any interpretation may influence orchestration.
capabilities.authority_role: Zero insurance authority. This boundary may propose request meaning only; it cannot establish policy facts, coverage, claim admissibility, approval, rejection, payment, non-payment, recommendation truth, or publication authority.
safety_invariants: Provider output is always untrusted; only a deterministic validator may create the downstream-safe validated marker.

The GSI request builder derives strict structured-output schema only from caller-governed concept, intent, semantic-fact and scenario-slot IDs plus the existing closed deterministic status, outcome and authority domains.
Provider output may use only caller-supplied governed identifiers; invented identifiers fail closed before validation.
Provider output cannot supply provenance or a resolution threshold; trusted provenance is adapter-owned and the deterministic validator owns the pinned governed confidence threshold.
AMBIGUOUS and UNRESOLVED interpretations cannot select a governed concept or request an executable semantic fact and must route to clarification.
RESOLVED interpretations must meet the governed validator threshold and may not retain competing interpretations.
The executable requested-outcome domain is a closed allow-list; unknown or unreviewed outcomes fail closed.
Claim approval, rejection, admissibility, payment and non-payment outcomes are absent from the executable requested-outcome domain.

Every interpretation attempt carries interpreter/model/config/input-hash provenance in an execution-linked serializable audit artifact, including provider failure, malformed output and validator rejection.
A failed interpretation audit artifact cannot carry a validated downstream marker; malformed provider output may be represented only by a SHA-256 digest rather than trusted raw output.
The live benchmark requires explicit runtime credentials and model choice and records no raw provider output.
The provider-backed adapter remains disconnected from canonical orchestration until the separate live P1 genericity and quality gates pass.

The runtime capability contains no insurer, product or governed-concept-specific branches, examples, regexes, cue tables or post-processing repairs; concept-specific benchmark cases are evaluation data only.
capabilities.notes: P1B supplies strict structured output and a credential-gated live benchmark path while preserving zero authority and no canonical orchestration wiring. Actual live/held-back success remains unproven until a credentialed run is captured under issue #395.
